| [CLAIM-950](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-950.md) | The competence-restriction loop is demonstrable: in capacity dynamics where competence is learned by doing and decays with disuse, making reinstatement a threshold on capacity turns a restriction justified by a lack of competence into a self-perpetuating trap, because the restriction causes the decay that holds capacity below the reinstatement threshold; the trap has a recoverability deadline, and it is escaped only by a route strong enough to restore practice or by training that adds capacity directly | The assistant's, carrying out [LEAD-104](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-104.md) (2026-11-22). [CASE-364](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-364.md) writes and runs it. The finding: making reinstatement a threshold C_r on capacity closes [CLAIM-721](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-721.md)'s loop in the model. A party restricted below C_r with no route to practice or training decays monotonically, never reaches C_r, and so is never reinstated — the restriction manufactures the evidence that extends it. The trap has a recoverability deadline (1.98 time units at [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s parameters) past which even manual release fails, the twin of [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s substitution deadline. It is escaped only by a practice route that restores exercise above a critical fraction (which still cannot ignite a party below threshold) or by a training route that adds capacity directly and ignites from zero — [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s capacity-first/transfer distinction reached by restriction. Each of [CLAIM-721](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-721.md)'s three conditions is shown necessary.
